img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Slice the apple and eat with the nuts.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Slice the apple and dip into the peanut butter.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Toast the bread. Halve the avocado, scoop half out of its skin and mash it with a fork and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan and fry the eggs over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still a little runny.
Spread the mashed avocado over the hot toast, top with the fried eggs and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Toast the bread for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then leave it on a board.
Mash the avocado with the soft cheese and a squeeze of lemon until creamy, then spread it over the toast.
Stir the finely chopped chilli into the honey. Lay the smoked salmon over the avocado, drizzle with the chilli honey and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Drain the tuna and put it in a bowl with the diced avocado, halved tomatoes and finely diced onion.
Add the oil, lemon juice and honey and mix gently.
Serve over the baby spinach, sprinkle with the chopped nuts and have a toasted pitta alongside.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

n: Bacon and Broccoli Mac and Cheese

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Boil the fusilli pasta in a large pan of salted water for 10 minutes, adding the broccoli florets for the last 3 minutes. Drain well.
Meanwhile, fry the bacon in a little oil for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until crisp, then chop it into pieces.
Whisk the cornflour into the cold milk in a pan, then heat gently, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes until thick. Take off the heat and stir in the grated cheddar until melted.
Stir the pasta, broccoli and bacon into the cheese sauce, divide between two bowls and serve hot.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a cooked breakfast plate with eggs and bacon

m: Heat the grill to high. Grill the bacon for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until crisp and cooked through, then chop.
Meanwhile, heat a little oil in a frying pan, add the spinach and wilt it for 1 minute, then tip it into a bowl.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 3 minutes until the whites are set, and halve the plum tomatoes.
Top the spinach with the eggs, tomatoes and chopped bacon and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Heat the grill to high. Grill the bacon for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until cooked through and crisp at the edges.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper and scramble in a non-stick pan over a low heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until just set.
Warm the protein wrap in a dry pan for 30 seconds, fill it with the eggs and bacon, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Heat the grill to high and grill the bacon for a couple of minutes on each side until crisp, then chop it into small pieces.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan, add the eggs and cook gently, stirring, until scrambled. Fold in the bacon and season.
Warm the wrap in a dry frying pan, cut or fold it into two tacos and divide the egg and bacon between them.
Top with the sliced avocado and coriander and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Heat half the oil in a frying pan and fry the sliced bacon for 5 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Add the chopped onion and pepper and fry for 5 minutes more until soft.
While that cooks, roughly mash the avocado and spread it down the middle of the wrap, then spoon the bacon mixture alongside.
Wipe out the pan, add the rest of the oil and the beaten eggs, and stir gently over a low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until just set.
Spoon the eggs onto the wrap, crumble over the feta and scatter with the chopped coriander. Roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a cooked breakfast plate with eggs and bacon

m: Heat the grill to high. Grill the bacon for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until cooked through and crisp at the edges.
Lightly toast the bread if you like, then spread both slices with butter.
Layer the hot bacon onto one slice, top with the other, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Beat the eggs in a bowl with the grated parmesan and plenty of black pepper, and set aside.
Chop the bacon and put it in a cold frying pan. Heat over a medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp.
Boil the fusilli in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes, then drain, saving a mugful of the cooking water.
Add the chopped garlic and chilli flakes to the bacon for 1 minute, then tip in the pasta. Take the pan off the heat.
Loosen the egg mixture with a splash of pasta water and stir it through the pasta, adding more water a little at a time until the sauce is silky. Serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium to high heat and cook the bacon for 3 to 4 minutes on each side (about 7 minutes in all) until crispy.
Push the bacon to one side and fry the egg for 2 to 3 minutes until the white is set and the yolk is still runny.
Meanwhile blitz or stir the yoghurt with most of the coriander and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Warm the naans in the microwave for a few seconds until soft and spread them with the yoghurt mix.
Fill with the bacon and egg, scatter over the rest of the coriander and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a pink smoothie in a glass with a straw

m: Blend everything until smooth.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Put the oats and milk in a small pan and bring to a gentle simmer over a medium heat.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Slice the banana while it cooks.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the sliced banana and a drizzle of honey, and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a pink smoothie in a glass with a straw

m: Peel the banana and break it into chunks.
Put the banana, milk and Greek yoghurt in a blender and blend for about 30 seconds until completely smooth.
Pour into a tall glass and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Stir the oats, milk and half the Greek yoghurt together in a jar, cover and chill in the fridge overnight.
For the sauce, mash half the banana with the peanut butter and honey, loosening with a splash of milk until smooth and spoonable.
In the morning, slice the rest of the banana. Layer sauce and banana over the oats, top with the remaining Greek yoghurt and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Cook the rice following the packet instructions, usually about 12 minutes, then drain and keep warm.
Meanwhile, heat a little oil in a large frying pan. Fry the diced chicken breast with the chopped pepper and onion for 8 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is golden and cooked through.
Stir in the barbecue sauce and sweetcorn and heat for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbling.
Divide the rice between two plates, spoon the BBQ chicken over the top and serve.

n: Spiced Chicken Gyros with Cabbage Salad

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Mix half the yoghurt with 15g of the oil, the lemon zest and juice, garlic, cumin, paprika, oregano and chilli flakes. Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks, coat well in the marinade, cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
Thread the chicken onto metal skewers. Shred the cabbage finely and toss with the sliced onion, tomatoes, chopped coriander, the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt.
Heat the grill to high and line a tray with foil. Grill the skewers for 8 to 10 minutes on each side, turning until charred and cooked through with no pink inside.
Warm the pittas under the grill for 1 minute, slice the chicken off the skewers and pile into the pittas with the cabbage salad. Spoon over the remaining yoghurt and serve.

n: BBQ Chicken Wrap with Herb Slaw

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Rub the chicken breast with the smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat and cook the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest.

While the chicken cooks, shred the cabbage and grate the carrot into a bowl with a pinch of salt and massage for 2 minutes until softened. Stir in the yoghurt and mayonnaise, then the chopped coriander and finely chopped chilli.

Brush the chicken with the barbecue sauce and slice it. Spread the herb slaw down the middle of the wrap, top with the chicken and sliced avocado, then fold in the sides and roll up. Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Heat a little oil in a frying pan and fry the sliced chicken breast over a medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Take the pan off the heat and toss the chicken in the barbecue sauce. Shred the lettuce and grate the cheddar.
Lay the wrap flat, pile on the chicken, lettuce and cheese, then fold in the sides and roll up. Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Drain and rinse the kidney beans. Chop the red pepper and grate the cheddar.
Spread the beans, pepper, sweetcorn and cheese over one wrap and season with salt and pepper. Press the second wrap on top.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan and cook the quesadilla for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Slide onto a board, cut into wedges and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Soften the chopped onion and peppers in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the paprika, cumin, purée, tomatoes, beans and chickpeas and simmer for 25 minutes.
Serve on the cooked rice topped with grated cheese.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Tip the baked beans into a small pan and warm over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until bubbling hot. Grate the cheddar.
Toast the bread until golden, and butter it if you like.
Pile the beans onto the toast, scatter the cheese over the top and serve while hot.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the noodles following the packet instructions, about 4 minutes, then drain.
Heat half the oil in a wok over a very high heat and stir-fry the beef strips for 2 minutes until browned. Tip onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then stir-fry the broccoli, sliced carrot and chopped garlic for 4 minutes until just tender.
Return the beef to the wok, add the soy sauce and teriyaki sauce and toss through the noodles until hot. Divide between two bowls and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Fry the chopped onion in half the oil over a high heat for 5 to 7 minutes until soft and starting to colour. Add the garlic for a minute, then the mince, breaking it up until browned.
Stir in the paprika, chilli flakes and tomato puree for a minute, then add the tinned tomatoes and half a tin of water. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile quarter the cherry tomatoes and mix with the sliced spring onion and coriander for a salsa. Slice the avocado and squeeze over the lime.
Fry the sliced peppers in the rest of the oil for 3 to 4 minutes, add the drained beans and heat through. Cook the rice, then stir the peppers and beans through it.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the chilli, salsa, avocado and a spoonful of yoghurt.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Roll the beef mince into 20 meatballs, put them on a baking tray and bake for 20 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Meanwhile soften the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, 300ml water and the crumbled stock cube, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Cook the spaghetti in boiling water for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Add the meatballs and sliced peppers to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until the peppers are tender and everything is piping hot. Serve over the spaghetti.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the noodles to the packet instructions, drain and set aside.
Stir-fry the sliced beef in half the oil over a high heat for about a minute until browned, then lift out.
Soften the sliced onion in the rest of the oil for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the mushrooms and garlic and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the stir-fry vegetables for a minute or two until piping hot.
Toss in the noodles with the soy sauce, vinegar and a splash of water, then the beef and spring onion, and cook for 2 minutes more.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Heat a large frying pan and brown the beef mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until no pink remains.
Stir in the fajita seasoning, crushed garlic and tomato purée, then add the drained kidney beans and a splash of water. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick and saucy, and cooked through.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave. Shred the lettuce, halve the tomatoes and grate the cheddar.
Spoon the beef into the tortillas, top with lettuce, tomatoes, cheese and a spoon of Greek yoghurt, and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola

m: Spoon the yogurt over the blueberries.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Tip the frozen fruit into a small pan with a splash of water and heat for 5 minutes, mashing it down until it breaks into a thick compote. Let it cool a little.
Stir the oats, soft cheese, Greek yoghurt, milk and honey together in a jar until smooth and well combined.
Spoon the compote over the top, cover and chill in the fridge overnight so the oats soften.
In the morning give it a quick stir if you like and serve cold.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Stir the oats, Greek yoghurt and milk together in a jar or bowl until well mixed.
Add the frozen fruit and a drizzle of honey, then cover and chill in the fridge overnight. The fruit thaws into a sauce.
In the morning give it a stir, top with a little more honey if you like and serve cold.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Fry the bacon in a dry pan for about 4 minutes until crisp, then drain it.
Spread the mayonnaise over the bread and layer the lettuce, sliced tomato and bacon on one slice.
Top with the second slice, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Whisk the eggs, Greek yoghurt and flour together in a shallow dish until smooth.
Lightly toast the bread, then press it into the mixture for a minute until both slices have soaked up the liquid.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the soaked bread for 2 minutes on each side until golden.
Meanwhile put the blueberries and honey in a small pan, bring to the boil, then simmer for 2 minutes until soft and syrupy.
Lift the French toast onto a plate, spoon the blueberry sauce over the top and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Bring a small pan of water to the boil, lower in the eggs and cook for 6 minutes for a runny yolk.
While the eggs cook, toast the bread, spread with butter and cut into thin soldiers.
Lift the eggs out, sit them in egg cups, tap off the tops and serve with the soldiers for dipping.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Boil for 8–9 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool under cold water and peel.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Chop the wafer-thin chicken and stir it into the mayonnaise.
Pile the chicken mayo onto one slice of bread and top with the salad leaves.
Close with the second slice, cut in half and serve.

n: Crispy Chilli Beef with Peanut Sauce

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Cook the rice following the pack instructions. Mix the mince with the crushed garlic and chilli flakes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the mince for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking it up, until browned, crispy at the edges and cooked through.
Stir the soy sauce and peanut butter together with a splash of boiling water to make a loose sauce.
Boil the peas and broccoli in salted water for 3 to 4 minutes, then drain.
Divide the rice, crispy beef and vegetables between two bowls and spoon over the peanut sauce.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Cook the noodles following the pack instructions, then drain. Slice the mushrooms, shred the cabbage, grate the carrots and slice the spring onion.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the pork mince with the crushed garlic for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the mushrooms, cabbage and carrots and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring often, until the pork is cooked through and the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the soy sauce and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide the noodles between two bowls, top with the pork and vegetables and scatter over the spring onion.

n: Buttery Tomatoes on Cheese on Toast

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Butter one side of each slice using 10g of the butter and toast it butter-side down in a medium pan for a few minutes until deep golden. Grate the cheese and pile it on the untoasted sides.
In the same pan heat the oil, fry the crushed garlic for a minute, then add the chilli flakes and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the halved tomatoes, season and cook for 10 minutes until they have broken down.
Turn the pan to low and whisk in the rest of the cold butter in small cubes until glossy, then stir through the herbs.
Heat the grill to high and grill the bread for 2 minutes until the cheese melts. Spoon the tomatoes on top and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Lay half the basil leaves on one slice of bread, then add the sliced mozzarella.
Top with the sliced tomatoes and chopped sun-dried tomatoes and drizzle over the vinegar.
Finish with the rest of the basil and the second slice of bread. Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Fry the chopped onion, chilli and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the paprika, curry powder and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the diced sweet potato, then pour in 500ml hot water mixed with the crumbled stock cube and the lime juice. Simmer over a medium heat for 15 minutes until the sweet potato is tender.
While that simmers, cook the rice in plenty of boiling water for 12 minutes, then drain.
Add the cod in chunks and the halved tomatoes to the curry and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Spoon the rice into bowls, ladle over the curry and scatter with coriander to serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a baked potato with melted cheese and bacon

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Prick the potato all over with a fork and rub with a pinch of salt.
Bake the potato directly on the oven shelf for 60 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the inside is soft.
Warm the baked beans in a small pan for 3 minutes. Grate the cheddar.
Split the potato open, spoon over the beans, scatter with the cheese and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Slice the cheese and serve on the crackers.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Grate the cheddar and put the bread in the toaster.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan, add the spinach and wilt it for 1 minute, stirring.
Pour in the eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, drawing the edges in, until almost set. Scatter over the cheese and fold the omelette in half.
Slide onto a plate and serve with the hot buttered toast.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Butter both slices of bread and slice or grate the cheddar.
Layer the cheese, sliced tomatoes and salad leaves on one slice.
Top with the second slice, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Fry the chopped onion, peppers and beef mince in the oil in a large pan for a few minutes until the mince is browned.
Add the diced courgette and cook for 3 minutes more.
Stir in the tomatoes, smoked paprika, chilli flakes and oregano. Simmer on a low heat for 10 minutes.
Scatter over the cheese and serve from the pan, or heat the grill to high and brown the top for 2 to 3 minutes.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Boil the fusilli pasta in salted water for 10 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil in a pan for 5 minutes, then stir in the passata and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the drained tuna, sweetcorn and pasta.
Tip into an ovenproof dish and scatter over the grated cheddar cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden. Divide between two plates and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Slice the chicken breast and fry in the oil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Leave to cool a little.
Chop the plum tomatoes and cucumber, and slice the avocado.
Toss the salad leaves with the tomatoes and cucumber in a bowl, then top with the chicken and avocado and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Halve and stone the avocado, then scoop out the flesh and mash it with a fork and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spread the mashed avocado over the bread, then layer on the sliced cooked chicken and salad leaves.
Close the sandwich, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Dice the chicken breast and chop the pepper. Fry in the oil with the fajita seasoning for 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, then stir in the drained kidney beans and warm for 1 minute.
Lay two wraps on a board and spread with the chicken and bean mix. Scatter over the grated cheddar and top with the other two wraps.
Toast each quesadilla in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Fry the diced chorizo in a large lidded pan over a medium to high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until it has given up its oil and turned crisp, then lift it out and set it aside.
Add the chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces, to the chorizo oil and fry for 5 to 6 minutes until golden, then stir in the sliced peppers and the garlic and cook for 3 minutes more.
Stir in the paprika, tomato puree and rice, then pour in the stock made from the stock cubes and 600ml boiling water, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover, turn the heat right down and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the chickpeas and the crisp chorizo, heat through for 2 minutes and serve in bowls.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the rice following the pack instructions, then spread out to cool. Dice the chicken breast and slice the spring onion.
Fry the chicken in half the oil for 6 minutes, stirring, until golden and cooked through. Push to one side of the pan and scramble the eggs in the rest of the oil.
Add the cold rice, peas and soy sauce and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until piping hot.
Scatter over the spring onion and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Wash and dry the iceberg lettuce and shred it. Slice the plum tomatoes.
Spread the red pepper houmous over the wrap, leaving a small border, then add the sliced cooked chicken, lettuce and tomatoes.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Melt the butter in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the chicken breast chunks for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the sliced leeks and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the mixed herbs, a stock cube dissolved in 150ml hot water, and the mustard.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the yoghurt and season well, then tip into a baking dish.
Lay the pastry over the top, pinch the edges to seal and cut two slits in the middle. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the pastry is golden and the chicken is cooked through.
Steam the broccoli for 5 minutes, then serve it alongside slices of the pie.

n: Chicken and Pineapple Kebabs with Spicy Rice

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the grill to high. Thread the chicken thigh chunks, pineapple and quartered onion onto skewers, brush with half the oil and rub with the paprika, salt and pepper.
Grill the kebabs for 8 to 10 minutes, turning now and then, until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, boil the rice for 10 to 12 minutes, then drain well.
Heat the rest of the oil in a frying pan and fry the chopped spring onions for 2 minutes. Add the jerk seasoning and rice and fry for 3 minutes.
Serve the spicy rice with the kebabs, a spoonful of yoghurt and lime wedges.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Toss the diced sweet potato in half the oil with a pinch of salt and roast for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
Slice the chicken breast and toss in the paprika. Fry in the rest of the oil for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 4 to 5 minutes until tender.
Spoon the sweet potato, chicken and broccoli into a bowl and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Heat the oil in a saucepan over a medium-high heat and fry the bacon, chopped, for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp.
Add the garlic and fry for 1 minute, then stir in the tomato puree, chopped tomatoes and a mugful of boiling water. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Stir in the gnocchi and the roast chicken slices, torn up, and bring back to a simmer. Tip everything into an ovenproof dish.
Scatter the breadcrumbs and grated cheddar over the top and bake for 10 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Leave to settle for 2 minutes, then serve in bowls with a green salad.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Chop the potatoes, carrots and onion into chunks and tip into a large roasting tin.
Toss with half the oil and the herbs, season, and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the chicken thighs and chopped courgette, drizzle with the rest of the oil and roast for 30 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Divide between two plates and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Fry the bacon in a dry pan for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp, then drain it.
Mash the avocado and spread it over the wrap, then top with the spinach, shredded chicken, halved tomatoes and the bacon.
Roll the wrap up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan). Boil the broccoli in salted water for 3 to 4 minutes, then drain and leave to cool.
Season the chicken, put it on a baking tray and bake for 25 minutes until cooked through, adding the bacon for the last 10 minutes until crisp. Leave to cool, as this salad is not served warm.
Cook the rice to the packet instructions and let it cool a little.
Chop the lettuce, broccoli, chicken and bacon and put them in a bowl with the rice.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and honey together, toss through the salad and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Slice the chicken, peppers and onion into strips.
Tip everything into a large tray with the drained beans, fajita seasoning, tomato puree, oil, garlic and 2 tablespoons of water. Mix well and spread out in one layer.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers are soft.
Warm the wraps in foil on the shelf below for the last 5 minutes. Serve with lime wedges and a spoonful of yoghurt.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Fry the bacon in a dry pan for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp, then drain it on kitchen paper.
Spread the wrap with the mayonnaise, then top with the lettuce, sliced chicken, sliced tomato and bacon.
Roll the wrap closed, cut it in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Coarsely grate the broccoli, stalk included, into a deep baking dish.
Add the butter beans with their liquid, the crème fraîche, most of the cheddar and the finely grated garlic. Season, mix, then scatter over the remaining cheddar.
Sit the chicken breasts on top, season and drizzle with the oil. Bake for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the cheese is golden.
Cut the lemon into wedges and serve the traybake in scoops with a wedge for squeezing over.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Slice the chicken breast and fry in the oil with the fajita seasoning for 6 to 8 minutes until cooked through. Cook the rice following the pack instructions.
Warm the drained kidney beans and sweetcorn in a small pan for 2 minutes. Chop the plum tomatoes.
Spoon the rice into a bowl and top with the chicken, beans, sweetcorn and tomatoes. Scatter over the grated cheddar and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Fry the diced bacon, chicken chunks and half the garlic in half the oil over a medium heat for 5 minutes until the chicken has coloured.

Add the lemon juice and the stock cube dissolved in 150ml boiling water, mix well and simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the liquid has reduced to a glossy coating. Meanwhile cook the pasta for about 10 minutes and drain.
Heat the grill to high. Cut the bread into cubes, toss with the rest of the garlic and oil, spread on a tray and toast for 5 minutes until crisp.
Stir the parmesan and soft cheese into the chicken until heated through, add the pasta and stir until coated.
Season and serve topped with the croutons.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Stir the parmesan into the mayonnaise to make a quick Caesar-style dressing.
Shred the salad leaves. Lay the wrap flat and spread with the dressing, then top with the sliced cooked chicken and salad.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Stir the Greek yogurt and pesto together in a small bowl.
Butter the outside of the bread. Spread the pesto mixture over the inside of both slices, then layer the mozzarella, sliced chicken, tomatoes and basil between them.
Cook the sandwich in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat for 2 minutes each side, pressing down lightly, until the bread is toasted and the cheese just starts to melt.
Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Mash the avocado with the lime juice and a pinch of salt for a quick guacamole. Slice the peppers and onion, and cut the chicken into thin strips.
Fry the sliced chorizo in a dry pan over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the oil runs and it turns slightly crisp.
Add the peppers, onion and a little oil and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Stir in the chicken and fajita seasoning and stir-fry for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside.
Spread guacamole over each tortilla, spoon on the filling, a dollop of crème fraîche and the coriander, then roll up and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Chop the potatoes and sweet potatoes into chunky pieces, the onions into wedges and the peppers into strips, and tip everything into a deep tray with the oil.
Fry the diced chorizo in a pan until the oil runs, add the sliced garlic and herbs, then pour in the stock cube dissolved in 200ml hot water and the vinegar.
Season the chicken with the paprika, sit it on the vegetables and pour the chorizo stock over. Cover with foil and bake for 35 minutes.
Take the foil off and bake for another 20 minutes, until the chicken is golden and cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Serve with a spoonful of yoghurt, the chopped chilli, crushed almonds and a squeeze of lemon.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the pasta to the packet instructions, saving a mug of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the sliced chicken in half the fajita seasoning and fry in half the oil for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and nearly cooked, then lift out.
Fry the sliced onion with the rest of the seasoning in the remaining oil for 3 to 4 minutes, then add the peppers and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes.
Return the chicken with the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the passata, pasta and yoghurt and heat through, loosening with pasta water if needed.
Scatter over the grated cheese and serve. It is also good cold the next day.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Slice the chicken breast into strips and toss in the fajita seasoning. Slice the pepper and onion.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan until hot and fry the chicken for 6 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Add the pepper and onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened. Warm the wraps for 30 seconds in a dry pan or the microwave.
Spoon the filling into the warm wraps, scatter over the grated cheddar and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the rice following the pack instructions and spread out to cool. Dice the chicken breast and slice the onion, pepper and spring onion.
Fry the chicken in a little oil for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked through. Scramble the eggs in the same pan for 1 to 2 minutes, then set both aside.
Fry the onion and pepper for 3 minutes, then add the cold rice and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the soy sauce.
Return the chicken and egg to the pan, stir through the teriyaki sauce until piping hot, then top with the spring onion and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Put the salad leaves in a lunchbox or tub and add the halved tomatoes and sliced cucumber.
Chop the chicken slices and scatter them on top.
Add the houmous in a spoonful on one side and serve with a pitta, or put the lid on and keep it chilled for later.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Brush the chicken breasts on both sides with the oil, season and press them into the panko so they are coated all over. Place on a baking tray.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden and cooked through, then rest for 4 to 5 minutes and slice thickly.
Meanwhile cook the rice following the pack instructions, stirring in the sliced spring onions for the last minute. Warm the katsu sauce in a small pan for 5 minutes.
Peel the carrot and cucumber into ribbons and toss with the chopped chilli and a squeeze of lime.
Divide the sliced chicken between two plates, pour over the sauce and serve with the rice, the salad and the rest of the lime in wedges.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Blitz the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste in a food processor. Cook the paste in a large high-sided frying pan with the oil and 3 tablespoons of water for 5 minutes.
Stir in the korma paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant, then add the diced chicken and turn it through the sauce.
Add the chopped nuts and the stock cube dissolved in 400ml of hot water. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the basmati rice following the pack instructions while the curry simmers.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the Greek yogurt and scatter over the coriander. Serve spooned over the rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Chop the chicken slices and mix them with the mayonnaise.
Put the salad leaves down the middle of the protein wrap and spoon the chicken mayo on top.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Spread the butter thinly over the bread.
Mix the sliced cooked chicken with the mayonnaise in a bowl and season with pepper.
Pile the chicken mayonnaise and salad leaves onto the bread, close the sandwich and cut in half to serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cut each chicken breast in half through the middle, then flatten the pieces between two sheets of baking paper until thin and even.
Dust the chicken with the flour, dip it in the beaten egg, then press on the breadcrumbs mixed with a pinch of salt and pepper until fully coated.
Fry the chicken in the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes each side until golden, crisp and cooked through.
Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water to packet instructions, about 10 minutes, then drain and stir through the passata, garlic and herbs for 2 minutes over a low heat.
Divide the spaghetti between two plates, top with the sliced chicken and scatter over the parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Bring 500 ml water to the boil with the stock and add the chicken breast. Simmer gently for 12 minutes until cooked through, then lift out and shred with two forks.
Add the sliced carrot and the noodles to the pan and cook for 4 minutes until tender. Slice the spring onion.
Return the chicken to the soup, ladle into a bowl and scatter over the spring onion. Serve with the bread.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan). Season the chicken, put it on a baking tray and bake for 25 minutes until cooked through, then leave to cool, as this salad is not served warm.
Chop the chicken, pepper, cucumber, coriander and nuts into even pieces and mix in a bowl.
Dress with the vinegar and oil and toss vigorously.
Serve with a spoonful of cottage cheese on each portion.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Chop the peppers into chunky pieces, slice the garlic, finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and cut the chicken into 3cm pieces. Crumble the stock cube into 700ml of hot water.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat and cook the peppers for 6 to 8 minutes until starting to soften. Stir in the garlic and orzo for a minute.

Pour in the stock, then add the harissa, sun-dried tomatoes and chicken. Simmer, stirring now and then, for 12 to 15 minutes until the orzo is tender, the liquid has been absorbed and the chicken is cooked through with no pink left. Add a splash of water if it dries out.
Stir in the mascarpone and red wine vinegar and season to taste.
Divide between bowls and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Brown the chicken breasts in a hot pan with a little oil for 3 minutes on each side, then lift onto a foil-lined tray with the sliced pepper and a drizzle of oil.
Roast for 15 to 20 minutes until the pepper is soft and the chicken is cooked through with no pink.

Stir the stock cube into 700ml boiling water with the tomato puree, rice vinegar, honey and chilli flakes. Soften the diced onion in the butter for 4 minutes, then stir in the rice, chopped garlic, paprika and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice is tender and creamy.
Shred the chicken, stir it into the risotto with the roasted pepper and half the grated cheddar, and serve topped with the rest of the cheese and sliced spring onion.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the fusilli pasta in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and cool under cold running water.
Fry the chicken breast in the oil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Leave to cool a little, then slice.
Halve the plum tomatoes. Toss the pasta with the pesto, chicken, tomatoes and spinach, then serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Warm the protein pittas in a toaster or the microwave and split them open.
Spread the inside of each with the mayonnaise and fill with the chicken, salad leaves and sliced tomato.
Serve straight away, or wrap them and keep chilled for later.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Spread one side of each slice of bread with the mayonnaise.
Layer the chicken slices, salad leaves, sliced tomato and cucumber on one slice.
Top with the second slice of bread, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Cut each wrap into wedges, spread them on a baking tray and bake for 6 minutes until crisp.
Toss the salad leaves with the sweetcorn, the sliced chicken and the soured cream, then add a squeeze of lime.
Pile the chicken salad onto the crisp wrap wedges and scatter the cheese over the top. Serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Roast the chicken thighs on a tray with a little oil for 18 minutes until cooked through, then shred with two forks.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil, add the garlic, then the tomatoes, puree, oregano and stock cube in 300ml hot water. Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, then stir in the shredded chicken.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for a minute, then whisk in the milk gradually until smooth and thick for a white sauce.
Wilt the spinach in a colander with boiling water, rinse and squeeze dry.
Layer the chicken sauce, lasagne sheets and spinach in a dish, finish with white sauce and cheese and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Slice the chicken into strips, toss with the fajita seasoning and fry in the oil with the garlic for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Shred the cabbage and toss with the juice of one lime and half the coriander.
In a second hot pan, fry the sweetcorn until sizzling and charred in places, then stir in the drained beans and warm through.
Warm the wraps. Fill with chicken, slaw and the bean and corn mix, then top with yoghurt, the remaining coriander and lime wedges.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the rice following the pack instructions and spread out to cool. Dice the chicken thighs and grate the carrots.
Fry the chicken in half the oil for 8 minutes, stirring, until golden and cooked through. Add the carrot for the last 2 minutes.
Push to one side, scramble the eggs in the rest of the oil for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the rice, peas and soy sauce and stir-fry for 3 minutes until piping hot.
Slice the spring onion, scatter over the rice and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Fry the sliced onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the diced chicken and cook until sealed.
Stir in the tikka paste, passata and coconut milk and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve over the cooked rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Toss the chicken pieces with half the yoghurt, the tikka paste and the oil, then cover and chill for at least 30 minutes (overnight is fine).
Heat the grill to high and line a tray with foil. Grill the chicken for 7 to 8 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred and cooked through, then leave to cool a little.
Warm the wrap for a few seconds in the microwave and spread it with the rest of the yoghurt.
Top with sliced tomato, cucumber, coriander and the chicken, roll up tightly, slice in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Grate most of the cucumber into the yoghurt, mix well and season. This is your tzatziki. Slice the rest of the cucumber.
Season the chicken and rub it with half the oil. Heat the rest of the oil in a pan over a medium heat and cook the chicken for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Warm the wrap in a dry pan or the microwave and spread it with the tzatziki.
Top with the chicken, sliced tomatoes and cucumber, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Fry the sliced onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the tikka paste.
Add the drained chickpeas, passata and coconut milk and simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir through the spinach until wilted and serve over the cooked rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Brown the mince in the oil with the chopped onion and pepper until no pink remains.
Stir in the paprika, cumin, chilli flakes and purée, then the tomatoes and beans. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Serve over the cooked rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Rinse the rice, cover with twice its volume of water, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes. Leave covered off the heat for 10 minutes, then fluff.
Thinly slice the cabbage, garlic and spring onions. Stir-fry the pork mince in half the oil over a medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the cabbage, five spice, a pinch of salt and pepper and the teriyaki sauce and toss for 2 minutes, then set aside.

In the same pan fry the garlic and most of the spring onions in the rest of the oil for 2 minutes, then add the soy sauce, chilli flakes and the stock cube dissolved in 400ml water. Simmer for 4 minutes and season with the vinegar.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the pork, ladle over the broth and scatter with the last spring onions.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan). Cook the pasta until just tender, then drain.
Fry the chopped onion and pork mince in the oil for about 5 minutes until browned.
Stir in the fajita seasoning, tomatoes, drained beans and sweetcorn, then add 300ml hot water with the stock cube crumbled in. Simmer for a few minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the pasta, tip into a baking dish, scatter over the cheese and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the chopped onion and garlic for 3 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the beef mince with the cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and fragrant.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and kidney beans and simmer for 5 minutes until thick and the mince is cooked through, then season.
Warm the wraps, spoon the chilli into them, top with the coriander and a spoonful of yoghurt, then roll up and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Slice the chicken thighs and toss in the 5-spice. Cook the rice following the pack instructions.
Heat a wok or large frying pan until hot and stir-fry the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the stir-fry vegetables and a splash of soy sauce and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender.
Spoon over the rice and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Toss the chicken pieces in the cornflour with a little seasoning and set aside.
Fry the chopped onion in half the oil in a wok over a low to medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, then add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the curry powder and ginger and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the stock made with the cube and 400ml of hot water, add the soy sauce, bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes. Tip the sauce into a blender and blitz until smooth.
Wipe out the pan, then fry the chicken in the remaining oil until browned all over. Pour the sauce back in and simmer for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the peas for the last 3 minutes while you cook the rice following the pack instructions. Serve the curry over the rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Boil the chopped potatoes for 10 minutes until just tender, then drain and leave to cool. Cooking them ahead helps them crisp.
Fry the diced chorizo in a non-stick pan over a medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp and the oil has run.
Turn up the heat, add the diced onion and pepper and cook for a couple of minutes, then add the potatoes and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Add the spinach, chopped chicken and chilli flakes and fry for a couple of minutes, then season.
Meanwhile poach the egg in gently simmering water for 3 minutes until the white is set and the yolk is runny.
Top the hash with the egg, scatter over the coriander and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Fry the halved chorizo in a large lidded sauté pan on a high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, then lift out and pour off most of the oil.
Add the oil and sliced onion, cover and cook for 5 minutes, then add the sliced pepper and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the paella rice.

Stir the paprika into 800ml hot water with the crumbled stock cube, pour it over the rice and bring to the boil, then simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the seafood and chorizo, cover and cook for 3 minutes until the seafood is piping hot and cooked through, then add the peas and cook for 2 minutes.
Squeeze over some lemon, leave to stand for 1 minute, then serve with the rest of the lemon in wedges.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Spread the chips on a large baking tray and bake for 10 minutes.
Brush the cod with a little oil, lay it on the tray beside the chips and bake for 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and the chips are golden and crisp.
Boil the peas in a pan of water for 3 minutes, then drain. Serve the cod with the chips and peas and a squeeze of lemon.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Stir the yoghurt, mayonnaise, curry powder, honey and a squeeze of lemon juice together in a bowl, and season with salt and pepper.
Slice the chicken and dice the apple. Chop the nuts roughly, then fold the chicken, apple and nuts through the dressing.
Tear the salad leaves into a bowl with the spinach, spoon the coronation chicken on top and serve. For a packed lunch, keep the chicken and leaves apart until you eat.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Chop the chicken slices and stir them into the yoghurt with the curry powder and honey.
Lay the salad leaves down the middle of the wrap and spoon the coronation chicken on top.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola

m: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and top with the blueberries.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Cube the cucumber and stir through the cottage cheese.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola

m: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and smooth the top.
Pile the blueberries on top and scatter over a small handful of chopped nuts.
Eat straight away, or cover and chill for up to an hour to serve cold.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Blend the eggs, cottage cheese, flour and honey until smooth, then leave the batter to rest for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and spoon in the batter in small rounds, in two batches.
Cook for 3 minutes until bubbles appear on top, flip and cook for another 3 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Stack the pancakes on a plate and serve with a drizzle of honey if you like.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Top the rice cakes with cottage cheese and sliced cucumber.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Heat the oil in a saucepan over a medium heat, add the sausages and fry for 5 minutes until browned all over, then lift them out.
Pour in the tomatoes with the tomato puree, paprika, honey and a splash of water, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Chop the sausages into bite-sized pieces and stir them into the sauce with the drained beans. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the sausages are cooked through, then season.
Meanwhile poach the egg in a small pan of simmering water for about 3 minutes until the white is set and the yolk is still runny.
Spoon the beans into a bowl, top with the poached egg and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the fusilli in boiling salted water to packet instructions, about 10 minutes, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain and keep a mugful of the water.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and cook the diced onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken strips with the paprika, cumin, oregano, chilli flakes and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Tip in the fusilli and peas, stir through the soft cheese with a splash of the pasta water until creamy, season, then divide between bowls and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Stir the mayonnaise, yoghurt, crushed garlic, a squeeze of lemon juice and half the parmesan together, and season with black pepper to make a creamy Caesar dressing.
Rub the spinach with the oil and a pinch of salt for a minute to soften it. Chop the chicken slices and the coriander and toss them through the spinach with the dressing.
Pile the filling onto a slice of bread, scatter over the rest of the parmesan, top with the second slice and serve cut in half.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the spaghetti in boiling water to packet instructions, about 10 minutes, adding the courgette strips for the final minute, then drain and keep a mugful of the cooking water.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and cook the mushrooms and bite-sized chicken pieces for about 5 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the mushrooms are golden.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the creme fraiche, the lemon zest and the herbs, loosening with a splash of the reserved water.
Toss through the spaghetti and courgette, divide between bowls and finish with black pepper and the parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Brown the chicken thighs in the oil in a lidded ovenproof pan.
Add the onion wedges, sliced carrot, garlic and flour and mix well. Pour in 400ml hot water with the stock cube, add the mushrooms and herbs and bring to the boil.
Cover and bake for 40 minutes until the chicken and vegetables are tender. Prick the potatoes and bake on a tray alongside.
Stir the crème fraîche through the stew. Crush the potatoes with the butter and a pinch of salt and serve alongside.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Boil the fusilli in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain, keeping a mugful of the pasta water. Slice the chicken breast into strips.
Fry the chicken in a hot pan for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Add the chopped garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the crème fraîche and a splash of the pasta water, then the spinach, and cook for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts into a creamy sauce.
Toss the pasta through the sauce, divide between two bowls and finish with grated parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until the yolks are firm, then drain, cool under cold water and peel.
Halve the eggs and mash the yolks in a bowl with the Greek yoghurt, soft cheese, paprika, salt and pepper until creamy.
Finely chop the egg whites and stir them into the yolk mixture.
Toast the bread, pile the creamy egg on top, scatter over the chilli flakes and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Sear the pork steaks in the oil for 2 minutes each side, then roast on a tray for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through. Cover and rest.
Cook the pasta to the packet instructions and drain.

In the pork pan, soften the chopped onion and garlic for a minute, add the quartered mushrooms for a minute, then the stock cube in 200ml hot water. Simmer for 5 minutes and stir in the crème fraîche and herbs.
Toss the pasta through the sauce, top with sliced pork and grated parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan). Wrap the salmon in foil with a drizzle of oil, half the garlic, a squeeze of lemon, salt and pepper, and bake for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Meanwhile boil the fusilli in salted water for 10 to 12 minutes until just tender, then drain.

Soften the sliced leeks in the butter and the rest of the garlic for 5 minutes, stir in the flour, then add the milk a little at a time, stirring, until you have a thick creamy sauce. Stir in the yoghurt and mustard and season well with pepper.
Tip the pasta into an ovenproof dish, flake the salmon over it (check for bones), spoon the creamy leeks over to the edges and scatter with the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden on top, then serve in bowls.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the fusilli in boiling salted water for 10 minutes. Slice the garlic and add it to the pan with the spinach for the final minute, until the spinach wilts. Drain, cool for a few minutes, then squeeze out any excess water.
Chop the tomatoes. Stir the cottage cheese, red pesto, tomatoes and most of the parmesan through the pasta and spinach, and season well with salt and pepper.
Scatter over the rest of the parmesan and serve at room temperature, or pack into a container and chill for up to 3 days.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the noodles following the pack instructions, then drain. Crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Fry the beef mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and crisp at the edges and cooked through.
Add the garlic and frozen veg and stir-fry for 4 minutes until hot.
Toss in the noodles with the soy and teriyaki sauces for 1 minute, then divide between two bowls and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Slice each chicken breast through the middle to make two thin pieces and flatten them with a rolling pin. Press both sides into the breadcrumbs mixed with the grated lemon zest and herbs.
Steam or boil the green beans and broccoli for 5 to 6 minutes until just tender.
Pan-fry the chicken in half the oil for 3 to 4 minutes each side (about 6 minutes in all), until golden and cooked right through.
Warm the drained butter beans in the rest of the oil with the sliced garlic, simmering for 2 minutes, then take off the heat and stir in the yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve the chicken on the beans with the greens alongside.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Season the chicken thighs with salt. Fry in the oil over a medium heat for 6 minutes, turn, and fry for 5 to 6 minutes more until crisp, golden and cooked through. Lift out and leave to rest.
Slice the spring onion and chilli and stir with half the soy sauce, half the vinegar, half the honey and half the crushed garlic to make a quick topping.
Mix the tomato puree, chilli flakes, the rest of the soy sauce, vinegar, honey and garlic with 4 tablespoons of water for the sauce.
Boil the noodles for 3 minutes, then drain, saving a little cooking water.
Pour the sauce into the chicken pan and bubble for 1 minute, then toss through the noodles with a splash of the cooking water.
Slice the chicken, pile it on the noodles and spoon over the spring onion topping.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water. Toss the sliced steak in the cornflour with a pinch of salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok over a medium heat and fry the steak for 5 to 6 minutes until crispy and cooked through. Lift it out and keep to one side, leaving the oil in the pan.
Fry the sliced onion and peppers in the same pan for 4 minutes until soft, then add the spring onions, chilli and garlic and cook for 2 minutes more.
Stir in the honey, tomato puree, vinegar and soy sauce with a splash of water and cook for 1 minute until glossy.
Add the noodles and crispy steak and toss for 2 minutes to heat through, then divide between bowls and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Slice the cucumber into sticks and dip into the houmous.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Boil the noodles for 4 minutes, then drain and rinse well so the strands stay separate.

Meanwhile heat the oil in a wok over a high heat and stir-fry the pepper, carrots, ginger, garlic and chilli for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the cumin and curry powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Mix the peanut butter and tomato puree with the stock made from the cube and 150ml of hot water until smooth.
Add the drained noodles and peas to the wok and pour in the peanut mixture. Toss everything together, loosening with a splash of water if it is thick.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, toss again and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Soak the rice noodles in boiling water for about 10 minutes, or as the packet says, then drain. Mince the garlic, slice the chilli, onion and peppers, cut the spring onion into 4cm pieces and thinly slice the chicken.
Stir together the fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, dark soy and honey in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a large wok until very hot and stir-fry the garlic, onion, peppers and chilli for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until cooked through with no pink left.
Pour in the sauce, add the noodles and toss until coated, then mix in the spring onion.
Divide between bowls and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Mix the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes in a bowl. Toss the chopped chicken thighs through it, cover and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pan and fry the chopped onion, garlic and ginger over a medium heat for 10 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the stock made with the cube and 300ml of hot water. Add the marinated chicken and cook for 15 minutes.
Pour in any marinade left in the bowl, simmer for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, and cook the basmati rice following the pack instructions.
Scatter the nuts and coriander over the curry. Serve with the rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Boil the egg for 8 minutes, cool and peel, and serve with the tomatoes.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Hard-boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool them under cold water, then peel and chop them.
Mash the avocado and mix it with the chopped egg, the mayonnaise and a pinch of salt.
Spoon the egg mix onto the protein wrap, add the sliced tomato, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Hard-boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool them under cold water, then peel and chop them.
Mash the avocado in a small bowl with the finely chopped celery, a squeeze of lemon juice, the chilli flakes and a pinch of salt.
Mix the chopped egg into the avocado.
Toast the bread, spread the egg and avocado mix on top and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Lower the eggs into boiling water and boil for 9 minutes. Cool under cold running water, then peel.
Mash the eggs in a bowl with the mayonnaise, a pinch of salt and plenty of pepper.
Spread the egg mayo over a slice of bread, top with the salad leaves and the second slice, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Lower the eggs into boiling water and boil for 7 to 8 minutes. Cool under cold running water for a minute, then peel.
Halve the avocado, remove the stone and slice the flesh. Halve the tomatoes.
Arrange the avocado and tomatoes on a plate, halve the eggs and serve with a pinch of salt and pepper.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Heat the grill to high. Whisk the eggs and milk with a pinch of salt in a wide bowl, add the bread, push it down gently and leave it to soak for 5 minutes, turning it halfway.
Meanwhile grill the bacon for about 2 minutes on each side until crisp.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and fry the soaked bread for 2 minutes on each side until golden.
Put the bread on a plate, top with the bacon and drizzle over the honey to serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a cooked breakfast plate with eggs and bacon

m: Heat the grill to high. Grill the sausages for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, until cooked through, adding the bacon for the last 8 to 10 minutes, until crisp.
Meanwhile heat half the oil in a frying pan and fry the mushrooms and halved tomatoes for 5 minutes, then keep warm.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil for 3 minutes, and warm the beans in a small pan for 3 minutes. Toast the bread.
Serve everything together on a hot plate.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Mix the soy sauce and honey in a small bowl. Finely slice the chilli and grate the garlic.
Melt the butter with the oil in a wok or large pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic and chilli for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the cooked prawns and heat them through for about a minute on each side. Meanwhile boil the noodles for 4 minutes and drain.
Add the spinach and let it wilt, then toss in the noodles and sauce over a high heat for a minute or two until glossy.
Top with chopped nuts and sliced spring onion.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Slice the chicken thighs into strips and mix with the oil, oregano, 1 chopped garlic clove and the juice of the lemon. Leave to marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat the grill to high and cook the chicken for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until charred and cooked through.
Mix the Greek yogurt with the grated cucumber, a little crushed garlic, salt and pepper to make a tzatziki. Shred the iceberg and slice the tomatoes.
Warm the pittas under the grill for 1 minute, then fill with the chicken, iceberg, tomatoes and tzatziki and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water to the packet instructions (about 10 minutes), then drain and rinse under cold water until completely cool.
Meanwhile whisk the vinegar, crushed garlic and oregano together in a large bowl.
Add the drained chickpeas, halved tomatoes, diced cucumber, onion and pepper, and the crumbled feta.
Add the cooled pasta, toss everything together and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Toast the pittas for 1 to 2 minutes until warm and slightly puffed. Chop the cucumber and tomatoes.
Split each pitta open and spread the inside with the houmous.
Stuff with the cucumber and tomatoes, crumble the feta over and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola

m: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and drizzle with honey.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola

m: Spoon the Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Tip the frozen fruit on top and leave it for a few minutes, so it thaws into a juicy sauce.
Roughly chop the nuts, scatter them over and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Cut the courgette, peppers and onions into chunky pieces, toss them in a large roasting tin with the oil, herbs, salt and pepper, and roast for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile cook the rice following the pack instructions. Cut the halloumi into cubes.
Add the halloumi to the tin, turn everything over and roast for 12 to 15 minutes more, until the cheese is golden and the veg is tender.
Divide the rice between two plates, spoon the traybake over and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Slice the halloumi. Grate the carrot, slice the cucumber and rinse the spinach.
Fry the halloumi in a dry non-stick pan for 2 minutes each side, until golden.
Spread the wrap with the houmous, add the carrot, cucumber, spinach and halloumi, then roll up tightly, halve and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Beat the eggs with a pinch of pepper. Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat.
Pour in the eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until just set, as a thin omelette. Scatter over the ham and grated cheddar and cook for 1 minute more.
Warm the wrap for 20 seconds, slide the omelette on top, roll up and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Butter both slices of bread, right to the edges.
Layer the ham, slices of cheddar and the salad leaves over one slice and season with pepper.
Top with the second slice, press down, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Butter the outsides of both slices of bread. Grate the cheddar and tear the ham into pieces.
Put one slice buttered side down in a frying pan, top with the ham and cheddar and cover with the other slice, buttered side up.
Cook over a medium heat for 3 minutes each side, pressing down, until golden and the cheese has melted. Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Grate the cheddar and slice the tomato.
Lay the ham, cheese, salad leaves and tomato down the middle of the protein wrap.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Spread the wrap with the mayonnaise.
Layer the ham, salad leaves, sliced tomato and cucumber down the middle.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Slice the cucumber, salt it and leave it in a colander for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water. Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Chop most of the coriander, keeping a few leaves back. Mix the turkey mince with the oregano, half the harissa, salt and pepper and shape into about 10 small meatballs with wet hands.
Put the meatballs on a lined tray, brush with the oil and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
Slice the red pepper and toss it with the cucumber, a squeeze of lemon juice and the grated zest.
Spread the yoghurt on plates and swirl in the remaining harissa. Warm the pittas, cut into triangles, and serve with the meatballs, salad and reserved coriander.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan and cook the sliced celery and chopped onion for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until softened. Meanwhile boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente.
Stir the chilli flakes, grated garlic, lemon zest and lemon juice into the softened vegetables, then add the tomato puree and cook briefly, stirring all the time.
Drain the spaghetti, keeping a mugful of the cooking water. Add the seafood to the sauce and warm it through for 2 to 3 minutes.
Toss the spaghetti into the sauce with the chopped basil and just enough of the cooking water to loosen it. Season and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Finely chop the spring onions and coriander and stir them into the mayonnaise with a good squeeze of lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toast the bread and let it cool a moment. Slice the chicken, cucumber and tomatoes, and season the tomatoes with a pinch of salt.
Spread herby mayonnaise on both slices of toast. Layer the cucumber, chicken, tomatoes and salad leaves on one, close the sandwich, press down gently and serve cut in half.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the rice following the pack instructions. Slice the chicken breast into strips and chop the garlic.
Fry the chicken in a hot pan for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir the soy, honey and 100ml water together and pour into the pan. Mix a teaspoon of cornflour with a splash of cold water and stir it in. Simmer for 2 minutes until glossy.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes. Divide the rice and broccoli between two plates, spoon over the chicken and every drop of the sauce and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Heat the grill to high. Mix the honey, soy sauce, five spice, paprika and oil in a bowl and turn the sliced pork in it.
Lay the pork on a foil-lined tray and pour the leftover marinade into a small pan. Grill the pork for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until lightly charred and cooked through.
Boil the spare marinade for about 3 minutes until thick and glossy and spoon it over the pork.
Boil the noodles for 3 minutes, adding the stir-fry vegetables for the last 2, then drain and serve with the pork.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Cook the rice following the packet, about 12 minutes, then drain and keep covered.

Finely chop the chilli and stir it with the tomato puree, honey, soy sauce and a splash of water for a quick sriracha-style sauce. Slice the spring onions and garlic, keeping a handful of the spring onions back.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cut the chicken thighs into bite-size pieces and fry for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden.
Add the garlic and most of the spring onions and cook for 5 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and bubble for 3 to 4 minutes until sticky and the chicken is cooked through with no pink left.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the chicken and scatter over the reserved spring onions.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Cut the carrots into sticks and serve with the houmous.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Mix the lamb mince with the grated onion, garlic, cumin, salt and pepper and shape into 8 koftas. Slice the cucumber and tomatoes and shred the iceberg.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the koftas for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through with no pink.
Warm the pittas in a toaster for 1 minute.
Fill the pittas with the koftas, iceberg, cucumber and tomatoes, top with a spoon of Greek yogurt and serve.

n: Lamb Leg Steaks with Rosemary Potatoes

img.a: Illustrative photo: grilled meat on a white plate

m: Cut the potatoes into small chunks and boil for 12 minutes until just tender. Drain and let them steam dry in the colander.
Heat a griddle pan until very hot. Rub half the oil over the lamb steaks, season, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until cooked through to your liking. Rest on a plate.
Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan, then fry the crushed garlic, chopped rosemary, capers and potatoes for 5 minutes. Stir in the Dijon mustard.
Boil the broccoli and green beans for 4 minutes, then serve alongside the lamb and potatoes.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Heat the oven to 190C (170C fan). Mix the lamb mince with the oregano and sesame seeds and roll into 16 small meatballs.
Fry the meatballs in the oil for 4 minutes until browned all over, then move to a baking tray. Sprinkle the pittas with water and wrap in foil.
Bake the meatballs and pittas together for 6 to 8 minutes until the lamb is cooked through and the bread is warm.
Meanwhile toast the chopped nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes and cool. Toss the sliced onion and quartered tomatoes with the vinegar and honey, and ripple the harissa through the yoghurt.
Split the pittas and fill with the meatballs, tomato salad, harissa yoghurt and houmous, then scatter with the coriander and nuts and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 160C (140C fan). Heat 2 teaspoons of the oil in a large pan and fry the chopped onions and garlic for 5 minutes until soft. Turn up the heat, add the lamb mince and fry for 5 minutes until browned.

Stir in the cinnamon, oregano and tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Add the chopped tomatoes, the stock cube and 150ml boiling water and simmer for 20 minutes until thick and the lamb is cooked through. Season.
Meanwhile, heat a griddle pan until very hot. Slice the aubergines lengthways into 1cm slices, brush with the remaining oil and griddle for 2 minutes each side in batches until golden.

Melt the butter in a pan, whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer for 2 minutes until thick. Off the heat, whisk in the parmesan, nutmeg and then the beaten egg.

Layer half the aubergine, all the lamb, then the rest of the aubergine in an ovenproof dish and pour over the sauce. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until risen and golden. Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes in the meantime, drain, rest the moussaka for 5 minutes, then serve with the potatoes.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Soften the chopped onion and grated carrot in a pan for 5 minutes, then add the beef mince and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and puree with a splash of water and simmer for 15 minutes until thick and rich. Season well.
For the cheese sauce, whisk the cornflour into the cold milk in a small pan, heat gently for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until thickened, then stir in half the cheddar.
Layer the lasagne sheets, beef ragu and cheese sauce in an ovenproof dish, finishing with a layer of sauce, and scatter over the remaining cheddar.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling, then rest for 5 minutes and serve in generous slices.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of sausages, mushrooms and mashed potato
