m: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the beef mince and cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the puree and cook for 1 minute, then add the diced potatoes and carrots, the chopped tomatoes and 200 ml water.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes and carrots are tender.
Stir in the drained kidney beans and cook for 5 minutes until hot. Season to taste, then ladle into bowls and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of sausages, mushrooms and mashed potato

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the beef mince and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through. Stir in the grated carrot, peas and passata and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Meanwhile, peel and chop the potatoes, boil for 15 minutes until tender, then drain and mash with the butter and a little salt and pepper.
Spoon the mince into an ovenproof dish, top with the mash and rough it up with a fork. Bake for 20 minutes until golden on top.
Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon onto warm plates and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Toss the diced sweet potato in half the oil with salt and pepper, spread on a tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until soft and golden.
Rub the pork steaks with the herbs, the juice of the lemon and the remaining oil, and leave for 5 minutes.
Fry the pork in a hot pan for 5 to 6 minutes each side until golden and cooked through with no pink inside, then rest for 3 minutes.
Steam or boil the broccoli florets for 4 minutes until just tender. Serve the pork on the roasted sweet potato with the broccoli alongside.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Heat the oil in a pan and soften the chopped onion and carrot for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the cumin and cook for 30 seconds, then add the lentils, passata and 350 ml water.
Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils are soft and starting to collapse. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into a bowl and serve hot.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Heat the oil in a pan and soften the chopped onion and carrot for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the cumin and cook for 30 seconds, then add the lentils, passata and 500 ml hot stock.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils are soft and starting to collapse. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into a bowl and serve with the bread on the side for dunking.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Cook the rice following the packet instructions and keep warm. Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the diced chicken and cook for 5 minutes, turning, until sealed and lightly golden on all sides.
Stir in the tikka paste for 1 minute, then add the drained chickpeas and passata. Simmer for 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside.
Stir in the spinach for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted, season to taste, then spoon over the rice and serve.

n: Malaysian Coconut Chicken with Pickled Cucumber

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Slice the cucumber finely and mix with the rice vinegar, half the honey and a pinch of salt; set aside to pickle. Put the basmati rice in a lidded pot with 300ml cold water, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on very low for 10 to 12 minutes.
Heat half the oil in a wide lidded pan and brown the chicken thighs with half the curry powder, salt and pepper for 4 to 5 minutes each side.

Meanwhile blitz half the chilli with the onion, nuts, ginger, garlic, soy, the rest of the curry powder, oil and honey into a chunky paste. Stir it into the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add the juice of the lime and 100ml water, cover and cook for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, then pour in the coconut milk and cook for 1 minute.
Pull the chicken into chunks with two forks. Serve with the rice and pickled cucumber, scattered with the remaining chilli sliced into rounds.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oil and butter in a large lidded pan over a medium heat. Cut the chicken into small pieces, add to the pan and fry for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Sprinkle over the paprika, oregano, mixed herbs and chilli flakes. Stir in the garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the orzo, crumble in the stock cube and pour in 650ml hot water. Cover and cook for 12 minutes, stirring often, until the orzo is almost tender, adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Stir in the spinach, lemon zest and juice, mascarpone and parmesan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the spinach has wilted and the sauce is creamy. Scatter with torn basil and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Cut the potatoes into skinny chips and microwave them on medium-high for 7 minutes until just soft. Toss with half the oil, the paprika, mixed herbs, salt and pepper.

Oven method: heat the oven to 220C (200C fan), spread the chips on a large tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden. In an air fryer, cook at 190C for 20 minutes instead, shaking halfway.
Dice the chicken and fry it in the remaining oil over a medium heat for 7 minutes until golden and cooked through. Add the crushed garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the oregano, red pesto, soft cheese and 100ml water, then simmer gently for 3 minutes into a creamy sauce. Season to taste.
Pile the chips into bowls and spoon the creamy marry me chicken over the top.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the fusilli in boiling salted water for 10 to 12 minutes until al dente. Scoop out a mug of the pasta water, then drain.
Halve the tomatoes and shred the cooked chicken. Heat the grill to high.
Blend the cottage cheese, pesto, tomato puree, passata, garlic, chilli flakes and paprika until smooth, loosening with a splash of pasta water.
Tip the pasta, chicken and tomatoes into an ovenproof dish, pour over the sauce and stir until coated, adding more pasta water if it looks dry.
Grate the parmesan over the top and grill for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and bubbling, then serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Finely dice the onion and crush the garlic. Mix the mince with the oregano, mixed herbs, salt and pepper and roll into 12 small meatballs.
Fry the meatballs in half the oil over a medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Lift them onto a plate.
Boil a large pan of water with the stock cube dissolved in it and cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes, saving a mug of the water before draining.

Fry the onion and garlic in the meatball pan with the rest of the oil for 7 minutes until soft, then stir in the pesto, tomato puree and crème fraîche with a ladle of pasta water. Return the meatballs and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss the drained spaghetti through the sauce and serve topped with grated parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Peel and chop the potatoes and boil for 15 minutes.
Squeeze the sausagemeat out of the skins and mix with the mince, half the grated onion, breadcrumbs, egg and herbs. Roll into about 16 small meatballs and brown in half the oil.
Soften the remaining chopped onion and garlic in the rest of the oil, then add the baked beans and BBQ sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Put the meatballs in an ovenproof dish and pour the beans over. Mash the potatoes with the butter and milk, spread on top and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden, then serve with peas or greens.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Mix the beef mince with the cumin and a pinch of salt and roll into 10 small meatballs, then flatten them slightly.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan and cook the meatballs for 8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Add the sliced peppers and cook over a high heat for 5 minutes until softened and lightly charred.
Stir a squeeze of lemon into the yoghurt. Warm the wraps for 20 seconds in the microwave and pile the spinach and torn coriander into each.
Top with the meatballs and peppers, spoon over the lemony yoghurt and serve rolled up.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Mix the chicken with the oil, half the garlic, cumin, paprika, oregano, curry powder, the zest of the lemon and half its juice, plus salt and pepper. Air fry at 200C for 14 to 18 minutes until cooked through, shaking halfway. Or heat the oven to 220C (200C fan) and roast on a tray for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
Meanwhile put the couscous in a heatproof bowl, pour over 300ml boiling water mixed with the stock cube, cover and leave for 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir the Greek yoghurt with the remaining garlic and lemon juice. Chop the sun-dried tomatoes, dice the cucumber and tear the basil.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes and slice. Fluff the couscous with a fork, stir in the tomatoes, cucumber, basil and vinegar, then serve topped with the chicken and the garlic yoghurt.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oil in a large, deep frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the gnocchi and diced chicken breast and fry for 5 minutes, turning, to brown the outside.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, sliced mixed peppers and trimmed green beans, then add a good splash of water.
Simmer for 6 minutes until the gnocchi is soft and the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside.
Heat the grill to high. Scatter the mozzarella over the pan and grill for 3 minutes until melted and golden, then serve straight from the pan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Brown the chicken thighs in the oil in a lidded pan, then add the chopped onion, grated carrot and paprika.
Stir in the rice and 450 ml hot stock, cover and cook on a low heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir through the peas for the last 3 minutes.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Slice the chicken and marinate it with half the fish sauce and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes. Mince the garlic and cut the broccoli into 3cm pieces. Soak the noodles in boiling water until soft, drain and toss with the dark soy.
Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, honey and the rest of the fish sauce for the noodle sauce. Stir the chopped chilli and a little rice vinegar together for a dipping sauce.
Heat half the sesame oil in a large pan over a high heat and sear the chicken for 2 minutes each side until golden. Remove it from the pan.
Add the rest of the oil and fry the garlic for 30 seconds. Scramble the eggs in big chunks, then add the broccoli, noodles and half the sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, adding more sauce, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until charred in places and the chicken is cooked through.
Divide between bowls and top with sliced cucumber, chopped nuts and the dipping sauce.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Dice the chicken into 1 to 2cm chunks and the onion finely, and cut the chorizo into small pieces.
Put the onion, chorizo and chicken in a non-stick pan over a medium heat, sprinkle over the paprika and fry for about 10 minutes until the onion is soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the tomato puree, take off the heat and mix in the soft cheese and grated cheddar.
Warm the wrap in the microwave, spoon most of the filling into the middle and fold in the sides and roll up, tucking the end under.
Put the wrap back in the hot pan, spread the rest of the filling on top and cook for a few minutes each side until golden and crisp. Leave for 5 minutes, then cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Slice the chicken into thin strips and toss with the mixed herbs, salt and pepper. Roughly chop the salad leaves and finely grate the parmesan and cheddar.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over high heat and fry the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile stir the mayonnaise, vinegar, crushed garlic and a splash of water into a dressing, then toss the salad in it.
Warm the wrap in the microwave for 10 to 15 seconds. Layer the chicken, dressed salad, parmesan and cheddar down the middle, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Return the wrap to the pan over a medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp, then serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Whisk the peanut butter, honey and milk together in a jar until smooth, then stir in the oats and the blueberries.
Cover and chill in the fridge overnight so the oats soak up the milk.
In the morning spoon the Greek yoghurt over the oats, top with the sliced banana and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Toast the bread for 2 minutes until golden.
Spread the peanut butter over the hot toast while it is warm so it melts slightly.
Slice the banana, lay it over the top and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Tip the oats and milk into a small pan and warm over a medium heat, stirring.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy, then stir in the peanut butter until swirled through.
Slice the banana, spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the banana and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Spread the rice cakes with peanut butter.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Toss the chicken thighs with the peri-peri seasoning and oil in a roasting tin.
Roast for 22 to 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
Meanwhile, microwave the buttered potato pouch following the packet instructions, and boil the corn cobs for 8 minutes until tender, then drain.
Serve the thighs with the potatoes and corn, spooning over any juices from the tin.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Toss the diced potatoes in the oil with salt and pepper and roast on a large tray for 15 minutes.
Chop the courgette and halve the plum tomatoes. Spread the pesto over the chicken breasts.
Add the courgette and tomatoes to the tray with the chicken, then roast for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside and the veg is golden.
Slice the chicken and serve with the roast vegetables and any juices from the tray.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the pasta for 10 to 12 minutes, then drain, keeping a little of the water.
Meanwhile fry the sliced courgette in the oil for 5 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Add the chopped chicken and diced tomatoes and warm through for a couple of minutes.
Toss everything with the pasta and pesto, loosening with a splash of pasta water, and top with shavings of parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Slice the potatoes thinly and cut the onion into wedges.
Tip the potatoes, onion, tomatoes, spring onions and sausage chunks into a large tray with the oil. Roast for 20 minutes, until the sausages are browned.
Stir in the drained beans and the stock cube dissolved in 200ml hot water, with lemon wedges alongside.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes more until the potatoes are tender and the sausages are cooked through.
Swirl through the pesto and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Cut the potatoes into small chunks and microwave for 4 minutes, then fry in the oil over a medium-high heat for 12 minutes with the paprika, salt and pepper until crisp. Tip out and keep warm.
In the same pan cook the pork mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through. Stir in the tomato puree and set aside, then wipe the pan.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper. Melt the butter over a low heat, add the eggs and stir gently for 3 minutes, taking the pan off the heat just before they look done.
Warm the wrap, spread with the BBQ sauce, then layer on the potatoes, eggs, pork and grated cheddar. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Brown the burrito in the pan for 2 minutes each side, rest for 5 minutes, then cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Slice the pork into 1cm strips. Mix the cornflour with a tablespoon of water and set aside.
Stir-fry the pork in half the oil over a high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until just cooked, then lift out.
Add the broccoli and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the rest of the oil, garlic and chilli for 2 minutes, then the sliced pepper for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir the soy sauce, half the honey and the cornflour mixture into the pan, return the pork and mix well.
Cook the noodles to the packet instructions, drain, toss with the rest of the honey and serve topped with the stir-fry.

n: Pork Steaks, Roast Potatoes and Veg

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of sausages, mushrooms and mashed potato

m: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Toss the chopped potatoes in half the oil with salt and pepper and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Rub the pork steaks with the herbs and the remaining oil.
Fry the pork in a hot pan for 5 to 6 minutes each side until golden and cooked through with no pink inside, then rest for 3 minutes.
Boil the mixed veg for 4 minutes and drain. Serve the pork with the roast potatoes and veg.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Halve and stone the avocado, scoop half into a bowl and mash with the mayonnaise and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spread the mash over the wrap, then top with the prawns and salad leaves.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly, then halve and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the rice to the packet instructions and drain. Boil the peas and green vegetables for 1 minute, then drain.
Fry the chopped onion in half the oil over a medium heat for 10 minutes until golden, then add the garlic for a minute.
Tip in the blanched vegetables and fry for 5 minutes, then add the cooked prawns and fry for 2 minutes until hot through.
Stir in the rice, push everything to one side and scramble the beaten eggs in the gap.
Fold everything together with the soy sauce and vinegar and scatter over the sliced spring onion.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Boil the broccoli florets in lightly salted water for 2 minutes until tender, then lift out and set aside. Cook the spaghetti in the same water following the pack instructions, then drain, keeping a ladleful of the cooking water.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan, add the bashed garlic and fry over a low heat for 2 minutes, then remove the garlic and discard it.
Add the tomatoes to the pan and fry over a medium heat for 5 minutes until soft and juicy. Stir in the prawns and heat them through for 2 minutes.
Add the harissa and the lemon zest and stir to coat.
Toss the spaghetti, a splash of the pasta water and the broccoli through the prawns. Season and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Mix the prawns with the mayonnaise and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Pile the prawn mayo onto one slice of bread and top with the salad leaves.
Close with the second slice, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Shred the iceberg, slice the cucumber and halve the plum tomatoes.
Tip the vegetables into a bowl and add the prawns.
Spoon over the Marie Rose seafood sauce, toss to coat and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the noodles following the packet instructions, drain and set aside. Heat half the oil in a wok and scramble the eggs for 1 minute, then break up and tip onto a plate.
Heat the remaining oil, add the stir-fry veg and cook over a high heat for 4 minutes until just tender.
Add the prawns and heat through for 2 minutes until piping hot, then add the noodles, teriyaki sauce and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Stir the eggs back in, divide between bowls and scatter over the chopped nuts to serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Stir the crushed garlic into the mayonnaise in a small bowl.
Spread the garlic mayo over the wraps, then add the shredded chicken, sliced tomatoes, cucumber and chopped lettuce.
Roll the wraps up tightly and serve, or pack them in a lunch box for later.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Take the Grenade bar and the protein yogurt pot from the fridge or cupboard.
Wash the apple and slice it if you like.
Serve the bar, yogurt pot and apple together as a no-cook snack.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of oats topped with sliced fruit

m: Blend the oats, banana, eggs and milk until you have a thick batter, and leave to stand for 2 minutes.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan over a medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of batter for 2 minutes each side until golden and set, in batches.
Stack the pancakes on a plate, spoon over the peanut butter and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: a pink smoothie in a glass with a straw

m: Peel the banana and break it into chunks. Measure the milk into a blender jug.
Add the banana, the isolate and the frozen berries to the milk.
Blend for 30 to 40 seconds until smooth and thick, then pour into a glass and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts
Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola
Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Dice the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 12 minutes until tender, then drain and leave to steam dry.
Put the salmon on a lined tray, brush with the oil and season. Bake for 12 minutes until it flakes easily.
Slice the cucumber and half the lemon, and tip the salad leaves into a bowl.
Flake the salmon over the potatoes, cucumber and salad leaves, squeeze over the lemon and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Slice the potatoes and boil them for 8 minutes, then drain. Cut the broccoli into florets.
Tear off two large squares of foil. Divide the potatoes, broccoli and salmon between them.
Drizzle with the oil, squeeze over the lemon, season and fold the foil over to seal each parcel.
Bake on a tray for 18 minutes until the salmon flakes and the potatoes are tender. Open carefully and serve in the parcels.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Roughly chop half the sweetcorn with the coriander and tomatoes and stir in the juice of one lime for a chunky salsa.
Shred the cabbage and toss it with the yoghurt, paprika, chilli flakes and the juice of the second lime.
Cut each salmon fillet lengthways into 3 strips. Fry in the oil for 2 minutes on each side (4 minutes in all) until golden and cooked through.
Warm the wraps for a minute. Fill with cabbage, salmon, salsa, sliced avocado and the rest of the sweetcorn, and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Mix the soy sauce and honey, place the salmon on a lined tray and brush the mixture over it.
Bake the salmon for 12 to 15 minutes until it flakes easily.
Meanwhile cook the rice following the pack instructions, usually about 12 minutes. Cut the broccoli into florets.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 4 to 5 minutes until tender but still bright green, then drain and toss with a little oil.
Divide the rice between two plates and top with the broccoli and salmon, spooning over any glaze from the tray.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Dice the chicken and toss it in the cornflour, five spice, salt and plenty of black pepper. Slice the pepper, onion and chilli, and chop the spring onions.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok and fry the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until crisp, golden and cooked through. Lift out onto a plate.
Stir-fry the pepper, onion and chilli in the same pan for 4 to 5 minutes until just soft.
Cook the rice following the pack instructions. Beat the eggs, stir them into the hot rice in the pan and cook for 2 minutes until set.
Return the chicken to the pan, toss everything together, scatter over the spring onions and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Cook the rice. Slice the chicken into strips, season and fry in the oil over a high heat for about 5 minutes until browned.
Mix the peanut butter, soy sauce, coconut milk and chilli flakes with the juice of one lime and a splash of boiled water.
Pour the sauce over the chicken, add the green vegetables and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, then stir through the rice until piping hot.
Serve with coriander and wedges of the second lime.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into 3cm cubes.
Brown the sausages and sweet potato in the oil in a large pan over a medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Turn the heat down, add the sliced onion, garlic, tomato puree and herbs and cook for a few minutes until the onion softens.
Add the drained beans and 250ml water, cover and cook for about 10 minutes until the potato is soft.
Finish with the grated lemon zest and a squeeze of juice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of sausages, mushrooms and mashed potato

m: Heat the grill to high. Grill the sausages for 20 to 25 minutes, turning often, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
Peel and chop the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender. Boil the peas for 3 minutes in the last part of the cooking.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter, the milk, salt and pepper until smooth.
Slice the onion and soften it in the oil for 8 minutes, then add a splash of hot stock and bubble for 2 minutes for a quick gravy.
Divide the mash between two plates and serve with the sausages, peas and onion gravy.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of sausages, mushrooms and mashed potato

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Chop the potatoes, carrots and onions into even chunks.
Toss them on a large tray with the oil, herbs, salt and pepper and roast for 15 minutes.
Chop the courgette. Add it to the tray with the sausages and turn everything over to coat in the oil.
Roast for a further 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the sausages are browned and cooked through and the potatoes are golden.
Divide between two plates and serve straight from the tray.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a cooked breakfast plate with eggs and bacon

m: Heat the grill to high. Grill the sausages for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through with no pink inside.
Warm the beans in a small pan over a low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set, and toast the bread.
Serve the sausages, eggs and beans together with the toast.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Brown the sausages in the oil in a wide, deep pan for 10 minutes, turning, then lift them out and cut each into 3 or 4 chunks. Meanwhile cook the rice to the packet instructions, drain and keep covered.
In the same pan, cook the chopped onion, celery, pepper, garlic and paprika with the chopped chilli, covered, for 10 to 15 minutes until soft.
Sprinkle over the flour and stir, then add the tomatoes, vinegar, sausage chunks and the stock cube dissolved in 350ml hot water, and bring to the boil.
Squash the tomatoes into the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Serve the stew over the rice with sliced spring onions.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and pepper and whisk with a fork until just combined.
Melt half the butter in a small non-stick pan over a low heat. Add the eggs and stir gently for 3 to 4 minutes until softly set.
Toast the bread and spread with the rest of the butter. Pile the scrambled eggs on top and serve straight away.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Soften the chopped onion and pepper in the oil, then stir in the paprika, cumin and tomatoes. Simmer for 12 minutes until thick.
Make wells in the sauce, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5–6 minutes until the whites are set.
Crumble over the feta and serve with toast.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Put the noodles in a bowl, cover with boiling water and leave for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water. Slice the onion and pepper, chop the chilli, crush the garlic and cut the green beans into thirds.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan until very hot. Add the onion, garlic and chilli and stir fry for 2 minutes, then add the curry powder and fry for 1 minute.
Add a splash of water, then the green beans and pepper, and stir fry for 4 to 5 minutes until just tender. Add the spinach and let it wilt.
Add the cooked prawns and heat them through for 2 minutes, then add the noodles and crushed nuts and toss everything together.
Take off the heat, splash over the soy sauce and serve in two bowls.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola
Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Lower the eggs into a pan of boiling water and boil for 6 minutes. Drain, cool under cold running water for 1 minute, then peel.
Meanwhile melt the butter with the smoked paprika and chilli flakes in a small pan over a low heat for 1 minute.
Toast the bread. Dice the avocado, toss it in the lime juice and spoon it onto the toast slices.
Break the eggs over the avocado, drizzle with the spiced butter, scatter over the coriander and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Lower the eggs into boiling water and boil for 8 minutes. Cool under cold running water, then peel and halve them.
Slice the cucumber and halve, stone and slice the avocado.
Arrange the smoked salmon, eggs, cucumber and avocado on a plate. Season with black pepper and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Split the bagel in half and toast the cut sides for 2 minutes until golden.
Spread the soft cheese generously over both halves while the bagel is still warm.
Top with the smoked salmon, add a twist of black pepper, close the bagel and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of pepper. Tear the smoked salmon into strips.
Melt half the butter in a small pan over a low heat, add the eggs and stir gently for 3 to 4 minutes until just set.
Toast the bread and spread with the remaining butter.
Take the pan off the heat, fold in the smoked salmon and spoon the eggs over the toast to serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Soften the chopped onions in half the oil for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the mince, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes, turn the heat up and brown for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up.
Dissolve the stock cube and tomato puree in 400ml hot water, pour into the pan and simmer for 5 minutes until thick and no longer wet.
Divide the mince between the wraps, roll up and place in an oiled dish. Top with the grated cheese and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Chop the tomatoes, spring onion and coriander with a splash of oil for a quick salsa and spoon over to serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Finely chop the onion, carrots and pepper. Fry the mince in a large pan over a high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned all over.
Add the chopped vegetables and the garlic and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, puree and herbs with salt and pepper. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mince is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water for 10 to 12 minutes, then drain.
Divide the spaghetti between two bowls, spoon over the bolognese and scatter with the parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Heat half the oil in a large saucepan, season the chicken thighs and brown them for 7 to 8 minutes, turning once, then lift out onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan with the chopped pepper, onion and garlic and fry for 8 minutes until lightly golden. Pour in the vinegar and cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the pan with the smoked paprika and the stock made with the cube and 400ml of hot water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the rice following the pack instructions while the stew simmers.
Scatter the nuts over the stew and serve with the rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Heat the oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat, add the chopped chorizo and fry gently for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the sliced onion and pepper and fry for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in most of the paprika, the cumin and the tomato puree, fry for a minute, then add a splash of water.
Pour in the tomatoes, bring to a simmer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until reduced slightly, then season.
Make two wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Spoon over the yoghurt, finish with a pinch of paprika and serve with two slices of toasted bread.

n: Speedy Chicken Noodle Soup with Egg

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Lower the eggs into boiling water and simmer for 6 to 7 minutes, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Dissolve the stock cube in 700ml boiling water in a pan, add the noodles and simmer for 4 minutes.
Stir the spinach into the broth for 1 minute until wilted, then add the soy sauce.
Ladle the noodles and broth into two bowls and top with the sliced chicken, the egg halves, coriander and a pinch of chilli flakes.

n: Spiced Chicken Sandwich with Herby Potatoes

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Cut the potatoes into bite-sized pieces, toss on a baking tray with half the oil, the oregano, salt and pepper and roast for 25 minutes until golden and crisp.
Season the chicken breasts with the chilli flakes, salt and pepper. Mix the sliced spring onion with the mayonnaise, chopped garlic, vinegar and a pinch of salt to make a garlic mayo.
Heat the rest of the oil in a lidded pan and fry the chicken for 3 minutes on each side until golden, add a splash of water, cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until cooked through with no pink.
Toast the bread on a tray in the oven for 5 minutes until hot, and shred the lettuce.
Slice the chicken, fill the toast with the chicken, garlic mayo and lettuce, and serve with the herby potatoes and the rest of the lettuce.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan). Cut the onions and peppers into chunky wedges and tip them into a large roasting tray with half the oil.
Rub the chicken with the paprika, cumin and chilli flakes, sit it on top of the veg and roast for 30 minutes until the veg is soft and the chicken is golden and cooked through.
Take the tray out, pour the rice around the chicken with 600ml boiling water, slice the sweetcorn into rounds and poke it in, then stir.
Cook for 20 minutes until the rice and chicken are tender, then turn the oven up to 200C (180C fan) for 5 minutes for a crispy top.
Serve with a spoonful of yoghurt on each portion.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Heat the oven to 210C (190C fan). Cut the onion into wedges, toss with the tomatoes and half the oil on a tray, and roast for 20 to 25 minutes until soft and lightly charred at the edges.
Meanwhile, boil the rice for 12 minutes, then drain. Fry the turkey mince in the rest of the oil over a medium-high heat for 10 minutes, breaking it up, until golden and crisp.
Stir the cumin, paprika, chilli flakes, tomato puree and half the grated garlic into the mince and fry for 5 minutes until fragrant and cooked through.

Mix the yoghurt with the remaining grated garlic, the juice of half the lemon and a pinch of salt. Slice the cucumber, chop the coriander and stir both through the roasted onion and tomatoes with a squeeze of lemon.
Divide the rice between two bowls, top with the roasted salad and spiced mince, and spoon over the garlic yoghurt.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Cook the rice following the pack instructions, usually about 12 minutes, then drain. Drain and rinse the kidney beans and chop the pepper.
Fry the pepper in the oil for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the paprika and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans and sweetcorn and heat through for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until piping hot.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, top with the spicy beans and scatter over the grated cheese.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Finely dice the onion and ginger, crush the garlic and thinly slice the chilli and spring onions, keeping the chilli and spring onions back for the top.
Cook the fusilli in boiling salted water following the packet, about 10 minutes. Save a mugful of the cooking water before draining.
Heat the oil in a large pan over a high heat and brown the mince in a thin layer for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through. Lift out and keep the juices in the pan.

Turn the heat to medium and soften the onion, garlic and ginger for about 7 minutes. Return the beef and stir in the tomato puree, gochujang, soy sauce and honey with a couple of ladles of pasta water. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the pasta and sesame oil, loosening with more water if needed, and finish with a squeeze of lime juice.
Divide between bowls and top with the spring onions, chilli and sesame seeds.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Start the rice following the pack instructions, about 12 minutes. Cut the chicken into 3cm pieces, chop the cabbage into large pieces and finely chop the garlic and chilli.
Heat the oil in a wok over a high heat. Season the chicken and fry for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and cooked through, add the garlic and chilli for 2 minutes, then lift everything out.
Fry the cabbage in the hot wok for 5 minutes until charred but still crunchy.
Return the chicken, add the soy sauce and honey and bubble for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Spoon the chicken and cabbage over the rice with the pan juices and scatter with coriander.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Slice the mushrooms, halve the tomatoes and beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a small ovenproof frying pan and soften the mushrooms for 3 minutes. Add the spinach and tomatoes and stir for 1 minute until the spinach wilts.
Heat the grill to high. Pour the eggs into the pan, scatter over the cheese and cook over a low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the base is set.
Put the pan under the grill for 2 minutes until the top is golden and set. Slide onto a plate and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Slice the spring onions and garlic. Soften them in the oil with a pinch of salt in a large lidded frying pan over a medium heat for 5 minutes.
Tip in the butter beans with their liquid, then add the spinach a handful at a time, letting each handful wilt for about 2 minutes.
Turn the heat down, stir in the lemon zest and crumble in most of the feta until creamy, adding a splash of hot water if it needs more sauce. Do not let it boil.
Cover and warm through for 3 minutes while you toast the pittas.
Top with torn coriander, black pepper and the last of the feta and serve from the pan with the warm pittas.

img.a: Illustrative photo: grilled meat on a white plate

m: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Spread the chips on a large tray and bake for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Take the steaks out of the fridge, pat dry and season well. Slice the mushrooms. Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan until very hot.
Fry the steaks for 2 to 3 minutes each side for medium, adding the butter for the last minute and spooning it over. Rest on a plate for 3 minutes.
Fry the mushrooms in the pan juices for 4 minutes until golden. Boil the peas for 3 minutes and drain.
Slice the steak and serve with the chips, mushrooms and peas.

img.a: Illustrative photo: grilled meat on a white plate

m: Boil the diced potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes, drain well and leave them to steam dry for 2 minutes.

Heat half the oil in a frying pan and fry the chopped onion and pepper for 5 minutes until soft, then set aside. Fry the potatoes in the same pan for 5 to 6 minutes until crisp, return the onion and pepper, toss and season.
Meanwhile heat a griddle or frying pan until very hot, season the steak and cook it for 3 minutes on each side, or longer until cooked to your liking. Rest it for a few minutes.
Wipe out the pan, heat the rest of the oil over a medium heat and fry the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Serve the sliced steak with the potato mixture and fried eggs.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Take the steaks out of the fridge, pat them dry, and season generously with salt. Drain and rinse the chickpeas and halve the tomatoes.
Finely chop the coriander and chilli and whisk in a large bowl with the grated garlic, chilli flakes, oregano, vinegar and 20g of the oil. Season, then stir in the chickpeas and tomatoes.
Heat a heavy frying pan until very hot with the rest of the oil. Sear the steaks, pressing down, for 2 minutes, then turn and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more. Rest for 10 minutes, then slice.
Toss the spinach through the chickpeas, top with the sliced steak and spoon over any resting juices.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Sear the sliced sizzle steak fast; set aside.
Fry peppers and onion; return steak with seasoning.
Serve with warm tortillas.

img.a: Illustrative photo: grilled meat on a white plate

m: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Spread the crispy potato slices on a tray and bake for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Take the steaks out of the fridge, pat dry with kitchen paper and season well with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan until very hot and sear the steaks for 3 to 4 minutes each side, then rest on a plate for 3 minutes.
Steam or boil the green vegetable medley for 5 minutes until tender.
Slice the steaks and serve with the potato slices and green vegetables.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Mix the turkey mince, half the sliced spring onions, half the garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, grated ginger, chilli flakes, half the soy sauce and the sesame oil, then shape into 10 balls.
Bake the meatballs on a lined tray for 16 to 18 minutes until golden and cooked through with no pink inside. Meanwhile boil the rice for 10 to 12 minutes.

For the sauce, put the honey, remaining soy sauce, garlic, the white of the remaining spring onions, the juice of half the lime and 100ml water in a small pan. Stir the cornflour with 1 tablespoon water, add it and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until thick and glossy. Stir in the green spring onion and half the sesame seeds.

Boil the broccoli for 3 to 4 minutes, then drain. Toss the cooked meatballs in the sauce until coated, then serve over the rice with the broccoli, the remaining sesame seeds and a wedge of the remaining lime.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Toss the chicken thighs with the barbecue sauce in a bowl and leave to marinate for 15 minutes, or longer if you have time.
Mix the chopped avocado, tomatoes, salad and shredded cabbage in a large bowl. Whisk the yoghurt, oil and vinegar with a pinch of salt and pepper, pour over the salad and toss.
Put the corn in a covered bowl with a splash of water and microwave for 4 minutes.
Heat a griddle pan over a high heat until very hot, then cook the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until charred and cooked through.
Cook the corn on the griddle for 5 minutes, turning now and then, until lightly charred all over.
Serve the chicken with the salad and corn, spreading the butter over the corn with a pinch of salt.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Split the bagel and toast the cut sides for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Leave the frozen summer fruits to thaw on a plate.
Whisk the soft cheese, Greek yoghurt, honey and a squeeze of lemon juice together until smooth.
Spread the cheesecake mixture over the warm bagel, spoon over the thawed fruit and its juices and serve.

n: Sweet Chilli Beef Skewers with Veg Rice

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for 10 minutes. Cook the rice to the packet instructions, about 12 minutes, then drain.
Heat the grill to medium-high. Toss the beef strips and halved tomatoes with two thirds of the sweet chilli sauce, then thread onto the skewers.
Grill the skewers for 6 minutes, turning once, until the beef is cooked through.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the baby corn, sugar snap peas and spring onions for 2 minutes, adding a splash of water to steam.
Add the rice and the rest of the sweet chilli sauce and cook for 2 minutes until hot. Serve the skewers on the rice with lime wedges and torn coriander.

n: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Curry with Naan

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Dice the sweet potato and drain the chickpeas. Heat the oil in a large pan and soften the sweet potato for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tikka paste for 1 minute, then add the chickpeas, passata and coconut milk. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the sweet potato is tender, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Stir through the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted. Warm the naans in a toaster or dry pan and serve with the curry.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Dice the sweet potato, chop the onion and deseed and chop the pepper.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the sweet potato for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the onion, pepper and paprika and cook for 3 minutes.
Make two wells in the hash, crack in the eggs, cover the pan and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set.
Season with salt and pepper and serve straight from the pan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork and bake for 45 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan and soften the chopped onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and drained kidney beans and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Split the baked potatoes, spoon over the chilli and top with grated cheddar to serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of sausages, mushrooms and mashed potato

m: Peel the sweet potatoes, cut into chunks and boil for 15 minutes until soft. Drain, mash and stir in the yoghurt.
Brown the mince in the oil in a large pan, then add the chopped onion and grated carrot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, crumbled stock cube, oregano and a splash of water and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Spoon the mince into a dish, top with the mash and grill or bake at 200C for 10 to 15 minutes until crisp at the edges. Serve with the peas.

n: Tikka Chicken Kebab with Green Bean Biryani

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Soak the rice in cold water for 30 minutes. Meanwhile mix the tikka paste and yoghurt in a large bowl, stir in half the chopped coriander, add the chicken thighs, coat well, cover and chill.
Melt the butter with the oil in a lidded pan and fry the sliced onion over a gentle heat for 6 minutes until soft and golden. Drain the rice and stir it in with the curry powder.
Pour in 750ml hot water with the crumbled stock cubes, add the green beans, bring to the boil, cover and cook on a low heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the grill to high. Lay the chicken thighs side by side with the long edges touching and push two long skewers through to hold them as one large kebab.
Grill the kebab for 20 minutes, turning the skewers a couple of times, until browned and cooked through with no pink where the thighs meet.
Spoon the biryani onto a platter, top with the kebab, scatter with the remaining coriander and serve with lemon wedges.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a colourful bowl of meat and vegetables

m: Cut the chicken into 3cm chunks. Mix half the yoghurt with the paprika, cumin, curry powder, tomato puree, crushed garlic and the lemon juice, then coat the chicken and marinate for 15 minutes.

Thread the chicken onto skewers. Oven method: heat the oven to 220C (200C fan) and roast on a tray for 15 minutes, turning once, until charred and cooked through. In an air fryer, cook at 200C for 6 to 8 minutes in a single layer.
Cook the rice following the pack instructions, about 12 minutes, then drain and fluff with a fork.
Mix the rest of the yoghurt with the chopped coriander, the lime juice, salt and pepper for a cooling dip.
Serve the skewers on the rice with the coriander and lime yoghurt spooned over.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the rice. Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool under cold water, peel and halve.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and fry in the oil over a medium-high heat for 6 to 7 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the garlic, teriyaki sauce and soy sauce with a splash of water and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until thick and glossy. Cook the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes.
Serve the rice topped with the chicken, peas and eggs, finished with sliced spring onion.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Slice the chicken breast into thin strips. Cook the noodles to the packet instructions, drain and set aside.
Heat a wok or large pan until hot and stir-fry the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the stir-fry vegetables and cook for 3 minutes, then pour in the teriyaki sauce and add the noodles.
Toss everything together for 2 minutes until piping hot, then divide between two bowls and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Brown the beef mince in a pan for 5 minutes until no pink remains. Set aside 2 tablespoons of the BBQ sauce, stir the rest into the mince with the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until cooked through and thick.
Heat the grill to high. Warm the drained kidney beans in the oil with 3 tablespoons of water for 3 minutes, then mash them coarsely with a fork.
Warm the wraps for 30 seconds in the microwave. Spread the beans down the middle of each, spoon on the beef and roll up into burritos.
Lay the burritos seam side down on a baking tray, brush with the reserved sauce, scatter over the cheddar and grill for 2 minutes until melted and golden.
Mash the avocado with a pinch of salt and serve it alongside the burritos.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of noodles with vegetables

m: Cook the rice following the packet, about 12 minutes, then drain and keep warm. Slice the pepper, onion, chilli and garlic, cut the green beans into 2cm pieces and pick the Thai basil leaves.

Slice the chicken, halve the slices and toss with 1 teaspoon of the fish sauce. Mix the rest of the fish sauce with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, dark soy and honey. Stir a little of the rice vinegar with some chilli for a dressing.
Heat half the oil in a large pan over a high heat and sear the chicken for 3 minutes until golden. Tip it into a bowl, it will finish cooking later.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the pepper, onion and chilli for 3 minutes. Add the garlic, then the beans with 2 tablespoons of water for 1 minute.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until thick and the chicken is cooked through. Off the heat, stir in the basil. Fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve the rice topped with the stir-fry, a fried egg, lime wedges and the dressing.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Cook the rice to the packet instructions, about 12 minutes, then drain and keep warm.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan or wok and stir-fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until golden, then lift out. Fry the chopped chicken thighs for 5 minutes until coloured all over.
Return the onion with the broccoli and sliced carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Stir in the curry paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and 150ml water and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Spoon the curry over the rice and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Boil the basmati rice for 10 to 12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Whisk the coconut milk with the curry paste, fish sauce and the finely grated zest of half the lime. Halve the sugar snap peas lengthways and toss them with the oil.
Divide the peas between two large sheets of baking parchment, set a cod fillet on each and spoon over the coconut mixture. Fold and seal the parcels tightly and place on a baking tray.

Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the fish flakes easily and the peas are tender. Open the parcels, squeeze over the juice of one lime, then serve with the rice, sliced chilli, coriander and lime wedges, spooning the sauce over.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Mix the turkey mince, sliced spring onions, garlic, breadcrumbs and egg in a bowl, then shape into 12 small balls.
Heat the oil in a large deep pan over a medium heat and fry the meatballs for 6 to 8 minutes until golden all over. Lift out onto a plate.
Boil the rice for 10 to 12 minutes until tender, adding the green beans for the last 4 minutes, then drain.

Fry the curry paste in the same pan for 2 minutes, then pour in the coconut milk and bring to a simmer. Return the meatballs and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until cooked through with no pink inside. Season with fish sauce and a squeeze of lime.
Divide the rice and beans between bowls, spoon over the curry and scatter with torn basil, coriander and sesame seeds, with lime wedges alongside.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 190C (170C fan). Quarter the tomatoes, cut the onion into wedges, season the cod and drizzle it with half the oil.
Tip the drained chickpeas into a small roasting tray with the coconut milk, tomatoes, onion and tikka paste, grate in the garlic, season and bake for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile boil the rice following the pack instructions, about 12 minutes, and drain. Stir the rice and peas into the tray, lay the cod on top and bake for 10 minutes more until the fish flakes easily.
Cut the lime into wedges and serve the traybake with a wedge for squeezing over.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Pour the tomato soup into a small pan and heat gently for 5 minutes until steaming hot.
Butter the outside of the bread slices and fill with grated cheddar.
Toast the sandwich in a frying pan for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted. Cut in half and serve with the soup for dunking.

img.a: Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Whisk the eggs together and season with salt and pepper.
Put the wrap in an oven-safe frying pan with the edges just turned up, pour the egg over it, and scatter over the chopped tomatoes, thinly sliced onion and grated cheddar.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the egg has set and the cheese is golden, then serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Drain the kidney beans and the tuna. Chop the tomatoes and cucumber and slice the spring onion.
Tip everything into a bowl and mix gently, breaking the tuna into chunks.
Dress with the oil and a squeeze of lemon, season with salt and pepper, then spoon into a bowl or box and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a baked potato with melted cheese and bacon

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Prick the potato all over with a fork and bake for 60 minutes until the skin is crisp and the inside soft.
Drain the tuna and sweetcorn and mix with the mayonnaise, a pinch of pepper and a little salt.
Split the hot potato, spoon the tuna and sweetcorn mayonnaise into the middle and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Mix the drained chickpeas, halved tomatoes, chopped cucumber, diced onion, lemon juice and oil in a large bowl with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Drain the tuna and stir it through gently with the crumbled feta.
Serve the salad with the pitta, toasted if you like.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Drain the tuna and mix it with the yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon juice, and season with black pepper.
Slice the cucumber into thin strips.
Spoon the tuna mix onto the protein wrap, add the cucumber, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook 60g fusilli; cool.
Mix a drained tin of tuna with 1 tbsp light mayo.
Toss with pasta, 40g sweetcorn and salad.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Drain the tuna and mix it with the mayonnaise and the finely sliced spring onion in a small bowl.
Pile the tuna mayo onto one slice of bread and top with the salad leaves.
Close with the second slice, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Drain the tuna and mix with the mayonnaise in a bowl. Spread over one slice of bread, top with grated cheddar and the second slice.
Butter the outside of the sandwich and fry in a pan over a medium heat for 3 minutes, then flip and cook for 3 minutes more until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut in half and serve while hot.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Mix the tuna with the mayo and pile onto the crackers.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white bowl of mixed nuts

m: Pile the drained tuna onto the rice cakes and top with sliced cucumber.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a baked potato with melted cheese and bacon

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Prick the potatoes all over with a fork and bake for 60 minutes until the skins are crisp and the insides soft.
Drain the tuna and sweetcorn and mix with the mayonnaise, a pinch of pepper and a little salt.
Halve the tomatoes. Split the potatoes, pile in the tuna filling and serve with the tomatoes on the side.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a white plate with fish and vegetables

m: Put the salad leaves in a lunchbox or tub and add the halved tomatoes and sliced cucumber.
Drain the tuna and sweetcorn and mix them with the yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Spoon the tuna mix on top and serve with a pitta, or put the lid on and keep it chilled for later.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Drain the tuna and sweetcorn and mix them with the mayonnaise.
Lay the salad leaves down the middle of the wrap and spoon the tuna mix on top.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Heat the oven to 190C (170C fan). Cook the pasta for 10 minutes, then drain.
Meanwhile soften the chopped onion, courgette and pepper in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the halved tomatoes, passata and herbs and simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix the pasta, sauce and drained, flaked tuna in a baking dish. Scatter over the grated cheese.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling, then serve hot.

n: Turkey and Bean Chilli with Rice

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the chopped onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the turkey mince and fry for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the paprika and cumin for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomatoes and drained kidney beans.
Simmer for 20 minutes until thick and the turkey is cooked through. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile cook the rice to the packet instructions and drain. Spoon the chilli over the rice and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of creamy soup with parsley and bread

m: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the chopped onion and carrot for 4 minutes. Add the turkey mince and fry for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the cumin for 1 minute, then add the passata and 300ml water and bring to the boil.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the turkey is cooked through and the carrot is tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into a bowl and serve hot.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Finely chop the onion, carrot, celery and mushrooms. Brown the turkey in the oil in a large pan, breaking it up, then set aside.
In the same pan, soften the vegetables and garlic for 5 to 8 minutes, then stir in the tomato puree for a minute.
Return the turkey with the tomatoes, passata, oregano and crumbled stock cube. Simmer gently for 30 minutes until thick, adding a splash of water if it dries out.
Cook the spaghetti to the packet instructions and serve topped with the sauce.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Grate the cheddar and slice the tomato.
Lay the turkey slices, cheese, salad leaves and tomato down the middle of the protein wrap.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three filled wraps stacked on a table

m: Lay the wrap flat and spread the soft cheese evenly over one side.
Top with the salad leaves, then the sliced turkey and a spoonful of cranberry sauce.
Fold in the sides and roll the wrap up tightly. Cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: three tacos with meat and lettuce on a white plate

m: Warm the protein pittas in a toaster or the microwave and split them open.
Spread the inside of each with houmous and fill with the turkey slices, sliced cucumber and tomato.
Serve straight away, or wrap them and keep chilled for later.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of curry with a spoon

m: Brown the turkey mince in the oil with the chopped onion until no pink remains.
Stir in the curry powder and tikka paste, then the passata and 100 ml water. Simmer for 15 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3.
Serve over the cooked rice.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water for about 10 minutes, then drain. At the same time, simmer the sliced peppers in a small pan with a splash of water and the lid on for 10 minutes until very soft.
Mix the turkey mince with the herbs, garlic and plenty of black pepper, then roll into small even meatballs.
Fry the meatballs in the oil in a large frying pan for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Blitz the soft peppers until smooth, pour them over the meatballs and heat through for 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the yoghurt to make a creamy sauce, then season to taste.
Divide the spaghetti between bowls and top with the meatballs and sauce.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a plate of roast meat and vegetables

m: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan). Mix the turkey mince with the egg, grated onion, herbs, salt and pepper and roll into 12 meatballs.
Chop the potatoes and carrots into bite-sized pieces, toss in the oil on a large baking tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the meatballs to the tray and roast for 20 minutes more, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Divide between two plates and serve straight from the tray.

img.a: Illustrative photo: penne pasta with a meat sauce

m: Mix the turkey mince with the egg, half the grated onion and the herbs and roll into 12 meatballs.
Brown in the oil, then add the rest of the onion and the garlic. Pour in the passata and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through.
Serve over the cooked spaghetti with parmesan.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a sandwich on a black plate

m: Spread one side of each slice of bread with the mayonnaise.
Layer the turkey slices, salad leaves, sliced tomato and cucumber on one slice.
Top with the second slice of bread, cut in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a pink smoothie in a glass with a straw
Illustrative photo: omelette on a plate

m: Slice the mushrooms and halve the tomatoes. Beat the eggs in a jug with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and fry the mushrooms and tomatoes for 3 minutes, then add the spinach for 1 minute until wilted.
Pour in the beaten eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until just set, then fold in half and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola

m: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and slice the banana.
Lay the banana slices over the yogurt and chop 15g nuts.
Scatter the chopped nuts on top and serve.

img.a: Illustrative photo: a bowl of yogurt with blueberries and granola

m: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Rinse the blueberries and pile 100g over the yogurt.
Scatter 30g granola on top and serve straight away.
